short: He took Britain into the Common Market and then lost an election to the miners.
full:
Edward Heath won an unexpected victory in June 1970 and achieved what had defeated Macmillan and Wilson: British entry into the European Economic Community on 1 January 1973, once de Gaulle's departure removed the French veto. A grammar school boy, organ scholar and ocean racer, he was also the first Conservative leader chosen by a ballot of MPs rather than emerging from the party's inner circle.

His government was overwhelmed by industrial conflict and the 1973 oil shock. A miners' overtime ban forced a three-day working week from January 1974 to conserve electricity. Heath called an election asking who governs Britain, narrowly lost, and left office in March. He had also imposed direct rule on Northern Ireland in 1972 and negotiated the Sunningdale power-sharing agreement, which a loyalist strike destroyed weeks after he fell. Margaret Thatcher took the leadership from him in 1975, and he opposed her for decades afterwards.
